title: Edificio de los Cinco Pisos, Edzná
summary: The Edificio de los Cinco Pisos is described by INAH as the most iconic monumental structure of the Maya city of Edzná in Campeche, Mexico. INAH says it is 31.50 m high with a base 60 m per side. Its earliest traces belong to the Petén phase of 200 to 600 CE, with later additions to about 1450.

uncertainty.note: Start is the beginning of the Petén phase (200-600 CE) whose traces INAH found at the foot of the south side; end is the close of the Postclassic remains (1200-1450 CE) in the upper levels. The building was enlarged in stages.

where.historical_name: Edificio de los Cinco Pisos in the Great Acropolis of Edzná, a Maya city

importance.justification: The most prominent structure of Edzná, a regional Maya capital between 400 and 1000 AD according to INAH.

footprint.description: Stepped base measuring 60 m per side from the central courtyard of the Acropolis; INAH says the original base, still unknown, is larger.

measurements.note: It reaches a height of 31.50 meters (INAH release reprinted by Brunoticias: 31.50 metros). INAH also prints 118 feet from the eastern plaza.
its base measures 60 m per side

phases.description: Built and enlarged in stages: Petén-phase traces (200-600 CE), Late architecture about 800 CE, Postclassic remains 1200-1450 CE (INAH release).
Clearing began in 1959 on the west side; INAH finished freeing all four sides in 2018.

reviewer_note: Shape stepped_pyramid. The second source is an INAH press release reprinted by a news outlet, so it is not fully independent of INAH. Coordinate is the Wikidata point for the Edzná site, not the building itself (about 0.5 km uncertainty). The phases leave a gap between 1450 and 1959 because no page opened describes its condition then. The name refers to five visible levels but the release counts nine.
